notes: Tag is named outright in the genre index, so Party & Casual with no second genre. I took Minigame over the Childhood Game preset even though the latter is literally modelled on tag: Childhood Game builds hiding props and a maze for hide-and-seek, which the author contradicted by asking for a clear readable grass field, while Minigame's lobby-plus-separated-stages structure with teleporters and a trigger row that names tagging is exactly this build. The genre notes warn that a continuous-space tag game does not need an isolated stage, but the author confirmed ten maps sharing one central lobby with a spinner picking the next one, so the P4 is earned by the ten maps rather than forced by the genre — the only preset option I dropped is spectator-zone, because tagged players sit down where they are on the field and are freed when their tagger is tagged, so nobody leaves the round. Deciding without a user: I added social-hub for the central lobby the spinner lives in, kept the leaderboard wall since a 30-player five-minute round is scored and nothing contradicts it, and treated the fill-in bots as player substitutes rather than ambient population, so they carry no option.
